en.askTitle: Put in your own degree, German level and offer and get the same fee check and first-year budget
en.runTitle: Da Nang to Germany: a 27-year-old nurse choosing between Triple Win and fee-charging agencies

fields.label: Age, degree and years of nursing experience
fields.value: 27, 4-year bachelor’s degree, 3 years of ward experience

fields.label: Agency or employer offer, with every fee and date
fields.placeholder: e.g. an agency offer with a €1,500 fee, payable on a stated date

fields.label: Target city in Germany
fields.placeholder: e.g. Leipzig, with your own rent and savings figures

en.template: Help me compare routes to a nursing job in Germany. I am {profile} in {city}, my German level is {level} and my target start is {start}. I was offered {offer}. Check it against the €2,000 cap, the no-advance rule and the written-information rule, list what I should ask for in writing, and rebuild the first-year budget for {target} with my own rent and savings figures. Flag anything unconfirmed. Ask before contacting anyone or paying anything.

phases.title: Read the official pages on recognition, German levels, visas, agency fees and Triple Win
phases.judgment: It checked before assuming Triple Win was an option: the Federal Employment Agency lists only India, Indonesia, the Philippines and Tunisia, not Vietnam. Vietnam’s fee law could only be read on a mirror site, so it is marked unconfirmed.

phases.title: Write the route guide and first-year budget, then recompute every figure
phases.judgment: A separate recalculation caught a wrong pre-departure subtotal (about €1,260; the right figure is €1,560.02) and small rounding slips in the Leipzig figures. Both were fixed.

workers: Read the German and Vietnamese rules on what agencies may charge, the WHO safeguards list, the Triple Win partner countries and warning signs of unfair recruitment
Read the official pages on visa fees and timings, German exam prices and dates, and what the Bavarian recognition office asks of Vietnamese nurses
